newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian MTBE - Soft amid weak gasoline, poor demand.
newsitem.headline: Asian MTBE - Soft amid weak gasoline, poor demand.

text.p: Asian MTBE prices were rangebound at low levels amid a softening gasoline market and weak demand, with Thai refiner Bangchak Petroleum Plc's tender to offer little support, industry sources said on Wednesday.
Free-on-board (fob) Singapore MTBE lifting end-April/May was steady, quoted at $260 to $270 per tonne.
"It is hard to say in the absence of of real deals," said one producer.
Regional demand continued to be thin with only a parcel of up to 1,000-tonnes sold last week at $277 per tonne, cost-and-freight Singapore for arrival end April.
Bangchak issued a tender on Wednesday to buy one 1,500-tonne cargo for any May delivery, which closes April 10 and is valid for a day.

Some traders expected the award level to be around the last award for an April 16-30 delivery cargo of 1,500 tonnes at $270-$275 per tonne, cost-and-freight Thailand, and from the same winner, Saudi Basic Industries Corp (SABIC).
"The last time SABIC slammed the market, but it did not show market direction -- that was already shown by gasoline," said a producer.

Unleaded 95-octane gasoline prices in Singapore have fallen in the last week by $1.80 per barrel to trade on Tuesday at $25.80, while on NYMEX unleaded gasoline has since March 19 lost around 6 cents per gallon to 61.55 cents.
"A lot depends on the gasoline," said one producer.

Traders said once the U.S. driving season starts, MTBE demand from there should also pick up and attract some cargoes. But at the moment no buyers were visble as Singapore fob prices needed to be around $250 before the arbitrage window opens.
"The U.S. market in May will be the support for the local market," a trader in Singapore said.

On the supply side, traders said there were ample cargoes but at least the start-up of the 700,000-tonne-per-year Sadaf plant, a joint-venture between Royal Dutch Shell and SABIC, was delayed until July.
The Saudi plant was originally due onstream in March, but a SABIC source said it would be running "any minute now".
